newsitem.title: ALGERIA: Bomb by Algeria school kills 10, wounds 20.
newsitem.headline: Bomb by Algeria school kills 10, wounds 20.

text.p: A car bomb killed 10 people and wounded at least 20 in a suburb of the Algerian capital on Sunday, security forces said.
The bomb went off around 7.30 a.m. (0630 GMT) near a coach parked by a school in Birkhadem.
Security forces described the attack as a "criminal action", the official Algerian term for attacks by Moslem fundamentalists.
The security forces, in a statement on the official Algerian news agency, gave no further details on the attack.
It was the second bombing in four days blamed on Islamists in an upsurge of violence ahead of a referendum to change Algeria's constitution.
Last Thursday, five people were killed when a bomb planted in a health centre in Boukiou village in western Algeria exploded during a visit by local council officials.
Algerians are due to vote on November 29 on changes to the constitution which would ban political parties based on religion and outlaw the use of violence as a means of gaining or holding power.
The run up to the vote has seen an increase of violence, with at least 78 people slaughtered in three operations blamed on fundamentalists.

At least 31 people were slain, their throats cut and their bodies mutilated, in an overnight raid on a village last Tuesday. Another 10 women and three children died the same way in a village attack earlier this month. At least 34 people were killed late last month in a road block set up, according to the authorities, by rebels in the southern province of Laghouat.

Violence erupted in Algeria shortly after the authorities in January 1992 cancelled a general election in which Islamists had taken a commanding lead. Since then, more than 50,000 people are estimated to have been killed.
